title: 2 women to be charged with allegedly disrupting NParks' crow traps, Singapore News

 singapore 2 women to be charged with allegedly disrupting NParks' crow traps
 They were involved in separate cases in Bukit Panjang and Yishun An NParks crow trap deployed in a HDB neighbourhood. PHOTO: AsiaOne/Ong Chin Wee PUBLISHED ON November 17, 2026 10:39 PM BY Sean Ler Two women will be charged in court on Wednesday (Nov 18) for their alleged involvement in separate cases of mischief that disrupted the National Parks Board's (NParks) crow population management operations.
 Police said on Tuesday night that they were alerted to the cases in March and August respectively.
 The first case involved a 60-year-old woman who had allegedly cut the cable securing the netting of a crow trap deployed at the open field near Block 629 Senja Road. 
 The woman did so twice, on March 10 and 11, resulting in the trapped crows escaping.
 The second case involved a 74-year-old woman who allegedly blocked a crow trap at Block 161 Yishun Street 11 with a piece of cardboard on three occasions — on Aug 24 and 26 — preventing crows from entering.
 Both women were identified through investigations and with the aid of closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage, the police said.
 They will be charged with committing causing disruption to key service.
 If found guilty of the said offence, they could each face up to 10 years' imprisonment, a fine, or both.
 The police warned would-be perpetrators that they take a serious view of such acts of mischief and will not hesitate to take firm action against those who damage public property or any apparatus deployed to serve public functions.
